correctness.rationale: Every subset of the thirty vertices up to size six is tested for a valid distance signature or all-pairs separation. Exactly 32,460 six-bases are enumerated. Two different constructions independently enumerate their jump and slide graphs. Explicitly verified S6/transvection actions partition all 32,460 bases into 62 orbits; one full BFS per orbit representative covers every starting state because these actions preserve adjacency and distance, establishing both complete eccentricity spectra and connectedness. Both complete provided programs were successfully replayed and outputs captured. This is a finite computation, not an extrapolation to other graphs.

originality.rationale: The prior known metric dimension 6 is excluded. Bailey (arXiv:1312.4973v1, §3 and the tables in §4) reports the minimum only, not a census of all minimum resolving sets or either relocation graph. Bartoli et al. (arXiv:1706.06583v1, generalized-quadrangle section) gives bounds, not these finite dynamics. The exact 32,460-count, 403,020/55,440-edge pair, radii/diameters, and distinguished 720-state orbit were compared as implications; none of the inspected primary results yields them. Search nonhits alone are not novelty proofs; a relevant recent thesis remains inaccessible and is disclosed.

value.rationale: The thirty-vertex GQ(2,2) incidence graph is a standard extremal symmetric test object. Resolving sets model optimal distance-based landmarks. Exact connectivity without additional landmarks and the sharp difference between move-local and unrestricted optimal relocation diameters (20 vs 8) address a motivated configuration-space question beyond the already tabulated minimum size. The exceptional S6 orbit provides a natural structural stratification rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
